title: multipart: add per-part/file size guards, content-type validation, and OpenAI-compat field mapping
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: customers using the OpenAI-compatibility layer and the tool/function-calling endpoints were able to upload large multipart payloads and malformed parts which caused OOMs and destabilized streaming. This PR centralizes multipart validation into the API gateway handler and adds explicit per-part and total payload limits, content-type sniffing, and dual-field support for OpenAI-compat clients (accept both 'file' and 'files' form fields). The change is intentionally conservative: we validate before handing off to the streaming runtime so we can guarantee early rejection and deterministic error responses instead of mid-stream failures. Implementation highlights: 1) api/handlers/multipart_handler.py implements a two-pass scan: fast header-only pass to enforce per-part size and type heuristics, followed by a streaming handoff that preserves the original stream for allowed parts. 2) Introduced config flags (env) for PART_MAX_BYTES and MULTIPART_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES with sane defaults (10MB per part, 50MB total) and runtime metrics emitted for rejected uploads. 3) Content-type safety: we perform lightweight sniffing (magic bytes + declared header) to avoid accepting text/plain labeled binary blobs; for non-whitelisted types we respond 415 with structured error payload. 4) OpenAI-compat: map legacy form names and accept arrays and singletons to reduce client breakage. 5) Added unit and integration tests covering edge cases and a small e2e run that exercises the streaming generation + tool-call with an uploaded schema file. Checklist: - [x] Implement server-side validation and env flags - [x] Add metrics and structured error responses - [x] Add unit tests and integration e2e - [x] Update docs/compatibility and API reference - [x] Add a hotfix note for incident INT-4421 in changelog

review_comments: Aaron Lee: Nice consolidation. Can we make PART_MAX_BYTES default to 8MB to match older SDKs?
Priya Kaur: I kept defaults slightly higher (10MB) after spike showed tokenized schema files often exceed 8MB; but made it configurable via env so infra can match historic behavior.
Marta Gomez: Please add a log line at INFO for rejected uploads with the rejection_reason tag; it will help SRE triage.
Priya Kaur: Added metric + structured log in latest commit c5a2f90.
Samir Patel: Security nit: make sure we don't emit file contents in logs.
discussion_resolution: Addressed reviewer feedback: defaults configurable, metrics/logs added, no file contents logged
release_notes: Server: multipart uploads now enforce per-part and total payload limits and validate content-type; clients that upload larger files should set PART_MAX_BYTES or switch to external storage and pass URLs. OpenAI-compat field mapping reduces client breakage for legacy integrations.
notes: This PR was motivated by an incident (INT-4421) where malformed multipart uploads caused worker OOMs. Post-merge, SLO for streaming stability improved in the subsequent canary run. Ops should consider setting stricter PART_MAX_BYTES in high-throughput clusters.
